# Intent: Disk Steward Reliability Repairs

Repair the review-confirmed Disk Steward reliability defects so users receive trustworthy, bounded disk evidence and safe local MCP integrations, without tests disturbing the installed app, without loss of user files or client configuration, and with regression and recovery evidence for the exact repaired candidate.

## Success Evidence

- `REQ-501` — Tests, duplicate launches, and shutdown cannot replace or remove another live application's endpoint or modify real user state.
- `REQ-502` — Published file evidence distinguishes observed presence, validated absence, stale and unavailable coverage across mutation, restart and scope changes.
- `REQ-503` — Monitoring makes measurable bounded progress and recovers database headroom without memory amplification or loss of authoritative current state.
- `REQ-504` — IPC, MCP and client-command execution have bounded work, output, deadlines and effective cancellation/revocation.
- `REQ-505` — All evidence tools export useful bounded and privacy-correct results with actual policy, accurate observation times and typed errors.
- `REQ-506` — Client setup preserves user modifications, is recoverable on partial failure, and distinguishes configuration from real app connectivity and task attribution.
- `REQ-507` — The repaired candidate has isolated CI, regression, scale, lifecycle and upgrade/rollback evidence; release readiness is reported separately from passing unit tests.

## Constraints

- Preserve native Swift/macOS 13, existing tool names where possible, and deliberate version/migration compatibility.
- No user-file deletion or delete MCP capability. Preserve live current-state truth and distinguish unknown from absent.
- Use isolated fixtures for tests; never open production defaults, safety state, watched roots or sockets in smoke/test mode.
- Keep safety budgets and crash-recovery controls; do not raise caps to conceal failure.
- Preserve prior completed Pyramid history; existing code is brownfield, not a greenfield project.
- Use one focused regression-tested patch per bounded change; no installed-app replacement, configuration migration, commit, push or release without separate user request.

## Non-Goals

- Whole-product rewrite or a new filesystem search engine.
- Whole-disk scanning or deliberate OOM reproduction on the user's Mac.
- General MCP marketplace, remote hosting, EndpointSecurity entitlement expansion or automatic cleanup.
- Automatically registering every MCP connection as a coding task.
- Guaranteeing zero bugs solely from a passing suite or publishing a release during this repair request.

## Assumptions

- `ASM-501` (medium) — A bounded durable traversal/publication design can meet useful progress and current resource budgets on representative 100k/1M workloads; must be measured before storage implementation.
